newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-For the Record: Highlights of RBA committee appearance.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-For the Record: Highlights of RBA committee appearance.

text.p: The retiring governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia, Bernie Fraser, and incoming governor Ian Macfarlane, appeared before a parliamentary committee on Thursday. They discussed economic conditions and the prospects for monetary policy. Here are the highlights:
Fraser -- "Can we grow faster? We probably can, given the spare capacity in plants and in the labout market."
"(Inflation and the current account deficit) are the two traditional constraints that have caused growth to slow down in the past. They're not constraints at the moment."

Fraser -- (Asked whether further rate cuts would be a consequence of economy needing further support) "Yes, that's right -- and if it could be accommodated in a situation where inflation was declining and the outlook for inflation was comfortable."
Fraser -- "We are a bit more confident about what might happen on inflation over the next six or 12 months than we are about what might happen to growth and employment."
Fraser -- "We agree generally with these (GDP and inflation) forecasts (in the budget), but we think inflation through 1996/97 could turn out to be a little lower."
Fraser -- "(The bank's recent rate cut and forecast for lower inflation) indicates that at least for the time being we think that wage increases are under control."

Macfarlane -- "... it would be extremely unfortunate if wage settlements, if the trade union movement were to aim for an average increase in wage settlements which was not consistent with that (the inflation target). I don't think they will."
Fraser -- "There's scope for the (U.S.-Australian) differential on bond yields to narrow further."

Fraser -- "Well you can ask a lot of people and you can get a lot of different answers, but I don't see any reason why we couldn't be aiming to get down to five or six percent and see what happens when we get there, if we get there."
